claims.text: Binder-based 3D ink-extrusion printing followed by isothermal sintering can be used to process AlCrFeNiSi powder.
In 3D ink-extrusion printing, a binder-containing green body is shaped before being densified by subsequent isothermal sintering.
The sintering step should be performed in an inert or reducing protective atmosphere.
Sufficient sintering time and temperature permit full inter-diffusion.
Full inter-diffusion and isothermal sintering enhance microstructural homogeneity.
The subsequent isothermal sintering step densifies the printed green body.
Binder-assisted printing decouples ambient-temperature shaping from thermal consolidation.
Binder-assisted printing creates a uniformly compacted green body.
The binder-assisted route avoids the rapid cooling associated with conventional rapid-solidification or laser-based processing.
Isothermal sintering minimizes thermal gradients and thereby reduces residual stress.
Controlled grain growth during sintering suppresses compositional segregation.
Controlled grain growth during sintering heals defects.
Printed and isothermally sintered AlCrFeNiSi will exhibit less compositional segregation than conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Printed and isothermally sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress than conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Printed and isothermally sintered AlCrFeNiSi will contain fewer pores and defect sites than conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Printed and isothermally sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have greater tensile strength than conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Printed and isothermally sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Rapid cooling in laser-based additive manufacturing or conventional bulk processing causes segregation, residual stress, and defects in AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention is most applicable when near-net-shape fabrication and precise control of sintering parameters are feasible.
The intervention's benefits may be limited in extreme-temperature or corrosion-dominated service environments.
